issues.description: setuptools<82 pin leaks into runtime install_requires of core package
issues.detail: The cap belongs in CI scripts where mmcv's broken build is the actual problem. Putting setuptools<82 in core/setup.py install_requires forces every downstream user of autogluon.core to downgrade setuptools at install time, for a bug that has nothing to do with their environment. CI hack contaminates the shipped package. Move it out.

issues.description: Three unrelated fixes smashed into one patch with an empty description
issues.detail: build_pkg setuptools cap, mmcv install rewrite, and core install_requires change are three separate concerns linked only by a shared FIXME URL. Empty PR description, no commit body explaining why. THREE-PATCHES. At minimum the commit message needs to state the failure mode, the root cause (pkg_resources removal in setuptools 82), and why each hunk is needed.

issues.description: mmengine downgrade from pinned git SHA to 0.10.7 silently drops the torch 2.5 fix
issues.detail: Previous comment said the git SHA was 'the fix for torch 2.5.' New code installs mmengine==0.10.7 from PyPI with no note about whether that release contains the fix or whether torch 2.5 support is still required. If 0.10.7 lacks the fix, this trades one CI failure for another. State it in the comment.

issues.description: Redundant setuptools<82 install before --no-build-isolation mmcv build
issues.detail: Line 8 pins setuptools<82, then line 9 builds mmcv with --no-build-isolation so it uses that setuptools. Fine. But mmdet on line 11 doesn't use --no-build-isolation, so the cap may not apply to its build env. Either justify why mmdet is safe or be consistent. Also no version pin on the pip-installed setuptools is questionable hygiene in a shared env.

issues.description: FIXME comments point to upstream issue but no tracking for revert
issues.detail: Two FIXME markers reference mmcv#3325 but nothing in the repo will remind the next maintainer to revert once that's fixed. A grep target is fine; an issue or TODO file entry is better. Six months from now someone will wonder why core ships with a setuptools cap.

review.summary: CI fix that does its job but bleeds into the shipped package. The setuptools<82 cap belongs in CI scripts and pyproject build-system requirements, not in autogluon.core's runtime install_requires where it punishes every downstream user for an mmcv build bug. Patch is also three unrelated changes with an empty description and a silent mmengine downgrade from a pinned git SHA whose stated purpose was a torch 2.5 fix. NEEDS-WORK: split, document the why, and keep the CI hack out of the published wheel.
